theory.intro: Restricting each trig function to a one-to-one piece gives three new functions. **$\arcsin x$** (also written $\sin^{-1}x$), **$\arccos x$** and **$\arctan x$** each return the one angle in that restricted piece whose sine, cosine or tangent is $x$.
facts: $y=\arcsin x$ has domain $-1\le x\le 1$ and range $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le y\le\frac{\pi}{2}$.
$y=\arccos x$ has domain $-1\le x\le 1$ and range $0\le y\le\pi$.
$y=\arctan x$ has domain all real $x$ and range $-\frac{\pi}{2}<y<\frac{\pi}{2}$.
The domain of an inverse is the range of the restricted function, and the range of the inverse is the restricted domain.
$\sin^{-1}x$ names the inverse function; it never means the reciprocal $\frac{1}{\sin x}$.
$y=\arcsin x$ and $y=\arctan x$ are increasing and odd, while $y=\arccos x$ is decreasing and is neither odd nor even.
$y=\arctan x$ has horizontal asymptotes $y=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $y=-\frac{\pi}{2}$; the other two inverses have no asymptotes.

workedExamples.question_text: State the standard domain restriction of $y=\sin x$ used to define $y=\arcsin x$. Sketch the inverse graph and state its domain, range, symmetry, monotonicity and any asymptotes.
State the standard domain restriction of $y=\cos x$ used to define $y=\arccos x$. Sketch the inverse graph and state its domain, range, endpoints, symmetry, monotonicity and any asymptotes.

State the standard domain restriction of $y=\tan x$ used to define $y=\tan^{-1}x$. Explain this notation, then sketch the inverse graph and state its domain, range, symmetry, monotonicity and asymptotes.
By swapping $x$ and $y$, find the inverse of $y=6+\cos x$ for $0\le x\le\pi$. State the inverse's domain and range.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Swap $x$ and $y$, then isolate cosine.

$\begin{aligned}x&=6+\cos y\\x-6&=\cos y\\y&=\arccos(x-6)\end{aligned}$

The original range is $5\le y\le7$, so the inverse domain is $5\le x\le7$. The inverse range is the original restricted domain, $0\le y\le\pi$.

workedExamples.question_text: By swapping $x$ and $y$, find the inverse of $y=7-6\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$ for $-\pi\le x\le\pi$. State the inverse's domain and range.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The restriction gives $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le\frac{x}{2}\le\frac{\pi}{2}$, so sine is one-to-one. Swap the variables and isolate sine before applying its inverse.

$\begin{aligned}x&=7-6\sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)\\x-7&=-6\sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)\\\frac{7-x}{6}&=\sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)\\\frac{y}{2}&=\arcsin\left(\frac{7-x}{6}\right)\\y&=2\arcsin\left(\frac{7-x}{6}\right)\end{aligned}$

The original range is $1\le y\le13$, so the inverse domain is $1\le x\le13$. The inverse range is $-\pi\le y\le\pi$.

foundation.question_text: State the domain and range of $y=\arcsin x$.
State the domain and range of $y=\cos^{-1}x$.
State the domain and range of $y=\tan^{-1}x$.
State whether $y=\arccos x$ is odd, even or neither.
State the equations of the two horizontal asymptotes of $y=\arctan x$.
foundation.solution_text:
The range of $y=\arctan x$ is $-\frac{\pi}{2}<y<\frac{\pi}{2}$, and the curve approaches both endpoints without reaching them.
$y=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $y=-\frac{\pi}{2}$

foundation.question_text: State whether $y=\arcsin x$ is increasing or decreasing.

development.question_text: State the coordinates of the two endpoints of the graph of $y=\arccos x$, and say whether the graph is increasing or decreasing.
development.solution_text:
The domain is $-1\le x\le 1$, so the endpoints are at $x=-1$ and $x=1$.
$\arccos(-1)=\pi$ and $\arccos 1=0$
Endpoints: $(-1,\pi)$ and $(1,0)$
The graph falls from $\pi$ to $0$, so it is decreasing.

development.question_text: State whether $y=\arcsin x$ is odd, even or neither, and whether it is increasing or decreasing.

Of the three inverse trigonometric functions, which one has domain all real numbers?
Explain why.
development.solution_text:
$y=\arctan x$.
The domain of an inverse is the range of the restricted function it undoes.
Restricted tangent takes every real value on $-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$, while restricted sine and cosine only take values in $[-1,1]$.

development.question_text: By swapping $x$ and $y$, find the inverse of $y=1+\cos x$ for $0\le x\le\pi$, and state its domain.
development.solution_text:
$y=1+\cos x$
$x=1+\cos y$
$\cos y=x-1$
$y=\arccos(x-1)$
The domain is where $-1\le x-1\le 1$, that is $0\le x\le 2$.
